why_it_matters: voxcraft-sim is the GPU engine the computationally designed organism literature actually uses; Kriegman et al. 2021 describe their simulator as 'a version of a voxel-based soft-body simulator modified to run on highly parallelized (GPU-based) computing platforms'. Building it would have been the strongest available check on everything else here.

target.pin_verified: git rev-parse HEAD matched; PIN-OK printed in every attempt
target.licence_of_record: CC0-1.0, read from the LICENSE file bytes at that commit: 'Creative Commons Legal Code / CC0 1.0 Universal'
target.licence_conflict: the project website cdorgs.github.io/code states the code is under Attribution-NonCommercial Creative Commons; the repository's own LICENSE file says CC0-1.0. Both are quoted; the conflict is NOT resolved in our favour, and a lawyer should look at it before anything from those repositories is redistributed. It does not block this page: we redistribute nothing, linking upstream and committing only our own driver and recipe.

platform: Nebius AI job, gpu-l40s-a, 1gpu-8vcpu-32gb, NVIDIA L40S

attempts.rationale: modern toolkit, forcing the target arch rather than autodetecting
the image voxcraft-sim's own Dockerfile pins, so the Boost and GCC the code was written against
attempt 2 could not configure because Ubuntu 18.04 ships CMake 3.10.2 and CMakeLists requires >= 3.12; this supplies a new enough CMake on the pinned toolchain

blocker_a_cuda.what: voxcraft-sim calls cudaDeviceSynchronize() from __device__ functions, which CUDA 12 removed.
blocker_a_cuda.first_error_verbatim: /tmp/voxcraft-sim/src/VX3/VX3_VoxelyzeKernel.cu(269): error: calling a __host__ function("cudaDeviceSynchronize") from a __device__ function("VX3_VoxelyzeKernel::doTimeStep") is not allowed

blocker_b_boost.what: independently, nvcc cannot compile Boost.Asio's trait machinery reached through boost::process when building VX3_SimulationManager.cu. This is an old-Boost-against-modern-GCC failure and is NOT a CUDA or GPU problem.
blocker_b_boost.error_verbatim: /usr/include/boost/asio/traits/static_query.hpp:85:47: error: ''indirect_ref' not supported by dump_decl<declaration error>' is not a template [-fpermissive]

1_modern_toolkit.note: both blockers are present in the same log; they are separate failures, not one described two ways.

2_pinned_image_as_shipped.what: could not even CONFIGURE. The pinned base image supplies exactly the stack the README names - CUDA 10.2.89, Boost 1.65.1, GCC 7.5.0 - but Ubuntu 18.04 ships CMake 3.10.2 while voxcraft-sim's CMakeLists requires >= 3.12.
2_pinned_image_as_shipped.ours_or_theirs: OURS. This is a gap in our environment setup, not a defect in the project, and it is why attempt 3 exists.

what_this_does_not_establish: that voxcraft-sim cannot be built. See attempts for exactly which toolkits were tried.
anything about whether its results agree with ours. No comparison was run and none is implied.
acceptance_as_declared: ./voxcraft-sim -i demos/basic/ -o output.xml -f produces a non-empty history file and exits 0.
process_note: Attempt 1's job reported COMPLETED while every build inside it failed, because the script ran to the end. The probe script now sets PROBE-VERDICT and exits 42 on a failed build, so the job's own status carries the result - attempt 2 duly reported FAILED. A COMPLETED job is not a result anyone has read.
